mistakes.quote: The journey that stands out is a trip I took
mistakes.correction: The journey that stands out is the trip I took
mistakes.note: Avoid unnecessary use of 'a' before uncountable nouns like 'trip' when it's already specified.
mistakes.practice: Rewrite 5 sentences with 'trip', 'journey', or 'experience' removing unnecessary 'a'.

mistakes.quote: I'd also argue that work has become more flexible, so it's easier to take time off.
mistakes.correction: I would also argue that work has become more flexible, so it is easier to take time off.
mistakes.note: While contractions are natural, in a formal context like the IELTS, using the full forms ('I would', 'it is') can demonstrate greater accuracy.
mistakes.practice: Rewrite 5 sentences using contractions, then rewrite them using full forms.
